concepts.def: The wartime partnership of the USA, USSR and Britain against the Axis, strained at Tehran, Yalta and Potsdam by disputes over Eastern Europe.
Between 1945 and 1949 the Iron Curtain, Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin Blockade and creation of NATO divided Europe into rival blocs.
Confrontations such as Hungary 1956, the building of the Berlin Wall in 1961 and the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 brought repeated danger of war.
Arms control agreements like SALT 1 and the Helsinki Accords eased tension until the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979 triggered a 'Second Cold War'.
Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika, the 1989 revolutions in Eastern Europe and the fall of the Berlin Wall preceded the dissolution of the USSR in 1991.
After 1991 the USA stood as sole superpower; the 9/11 attacks of 2001 led to wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, while Russia grew more assertive by 2010.

International Relations: Changing Superpower Relations 1941-2010 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What held the Grand Alliance together during the Second World War?
options: A common enemy - Nazi Germany
A shared belief in communism
A joint commitment to free elections everywhere
American membership of the Comintern

mcqs.q: What was Gorbachev's policy of glasnost?
options: Greater openness, allowing freer speech and criticism in the USSR
The rapid privatisation of all Soviet industry
A programme to build more nuclear missiles
The banning of religious worship

mcqs.q: Which event in 1979 helped end detente?
options: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
The Cuban Missile Crisis
The fall of the Berlin Wall
The outbreak of the Korean War
Al-Qaeda terrorists attacked the World Trade Center and the Pentagon
The USA invaded Iraq
The Soviet Union was dissolved
NATO was founded

mcqs.q: Were the USA and USSR natural friends who suddenly fell out after 1945?
options: The Cold War ended when both sides destroyed all their weapons.
The superpowers were close allies with no tensions until the Cold War began without warning.
No - the Grand Alliance was a marriage of convenience against Hitler; ideological rivalry dated from 1917 and resurfaced as soon as Germany was beaten.
The USA and USSR were joined in a single federation during the war.

mcqs.q: Did Gorbachev set out to destroy communism and the USSR?
options: Gorbachev was an American politician sent to reform Russia.
The USA and USSR were joined in a single federation during the war.
Gorbachev deliberately planned the break-up of the Soviet Union.
No - his reforms of glasnost and perestroika aimed to save the Soviet system, but they released criticism and national movements he could not control.

mcqs.q: Did the Cold War end because the USA defeated the USSR in battle?
options: The Cold War ended when both sides destroyed all their weapons.
The USA and USSR were joined in a single federation during the war.
A final military victory by the USA ended the Cold War.
No - the superpowers never fought each other directly; the Cold War ended through Soviet economic failure, Gorbachev's reforms and the revolutions of 1989-91.
